title: 167. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Expanding Products of Binomials
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Expanding a Product of Two Binomials with Positive Constants
questions.learningObjective: Expand the product of two binomials and combine like terms.
questions.question: Expand \((x+2)(x+3)\).
questions.explanation:
Use the distributive property:
\[
(x+2)(x+3)=x(x+3)+2(x+3)=x^2+3x+2x+6=x^2+5x+6
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2+5x+6\).
questions.hint: Multiply each term in the first binomial by each term in the second binomial, then combine like terms.

questions.concept: Expanding a Product of Binomials with a Negative Constant
questions.learningObjective: Expand a binomial product involving a negative constant and simplify.
questions.question: Expand \((x-4)(x+2)\).
questions.explanation:
Apply the distributive property:
\[
(x-4)(x+2)=x(x+2)-4(x+2)=x^2+2x-4x-8=x^2-2x-8
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2-2x-8\).
questions.hint: Pay attention to the sign when multiplying the negative constant by each term.

questions.concept: Expanding a Product of Binomials with a Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of binomials when one binomial has a leading coefficient.
questions.question: Expand \((2x+3)(x-5)\).
questions.explanation:
Use the distributive property:
\[
(2x+3)(x-5)=2x(x-5)+3(x-5)=2x^2-10x+3x-15=2x^2-7x-15
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(2x^2-7x-15\).
questions.hint: Multiply \(2x\) and \(3\) separately by each term of \(x-5\), then combine the \(x\) terms.

questions.concept: Expanding a Product of Binomials with Two Leading Coefficients
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials that both have leading coefficients.
questions.question: Expand \((3x-2)(2x+1)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each pair of terms:
\[
(3x-2)(2x+1)=3x(2x+1)-2(2x+1)=6x^2+3x-4x-2=6x^2-x-2
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(6x^2-x-2\).
questions.hint: Multiply both terms of the first binomial by both terms of the second, then combine like terms.

questions.learningObjective: Expand a binomial squared and recognize the perfect-square trinomial pattern.
questions.question: Expand \((x+5)^2\).
questions.explanation:
Write the square as a product:
\[
(x+5)^2=(x+5)(x+5)=x^2+5x+5x+25=x^2+10x+25
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2+10x+25\).

questions.concept: Expanding a Perfect Square Binomial with Subtraction
questions.learningObjective: Expand a binomial squared involving subtraction.
questions.question: Expand \((x-3)^2\).
questions.explanation:
Write the square as a product:
\[
(x-3)^2=(x-3)(x-3)=x^2-3x-3x+9=x^2-6x+9
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2-6x+9\).

questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of the form \((a+b)(a-b)\) and identify the difference of squares.
questions.question: Expand \((x+7)(x-7)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply the binomials:
\[
(x+7)(x-7)=x^2-7x+7x-49=x^2-49
\]
The middle terms cancel, leaving a difference of squares. Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2-49\).

questions.concept: Expanding a Difference of Squares with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Expand a difference-of-squares product involving two variables.
questions.question: Expand \((2x-3y)(2x+3y)\).
questions.explanation:
Use the difference-of-squares pattern with \(a=2x\) and \(b=3y\):
\[
(2x-3y)(2x+3y)=(2x)^2-(3y)^2=4x^2-9y^2
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(4x^2-9y^2\).
questions.hint: Square the first term and subtract the square of the second term.

questions.concept: Expanding a Product of Binomials with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials containing two variables and combine like terms.
questions.question: Expand \((3a+2b)(a-4b)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each term. Combine the \(ab\) terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(3a+2b)(a-4b) &= 3a(a-4b)+2b(a-4b)=3a^2-12ab+2ab-8b^2\\
-12ab+2ab &= -10ab
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(3a^2-10ab-8b^2\).
questions.hint: Multiply all four pairs of terms, then combine the two \(ab\) terms carefully.

questions.concept: Expanding a Product of Binomials with Positive and Negative Terms
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials with leading coefficients and combine like terms.
questions.question: Expand \((2x+5)(3x-4)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each pair of terms. Combine the \(x\) terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x+5)(3x-4) &= 2x(3x-4)+5(3x-4)=6x^2-8x+15x-20\\
-8x+15x &= 7x
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(6x^2+7x-20\).
questions.hint: Multiply the first terms, outer terms, inner terms, and last terms, then combine the \(x\) terms.
